newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: New Lithuania finmin backs money policy change.
newsitem.headline: New Lithuania finmin backs money policy change.

text.p: VILNIUS, Feb 20 (Reuter) New Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta backs the planned changes in the country's monetary policy that will eventually see the end of the currency board, newspapers quoted him as saying on Thursday.
Shemeta was appointed by President Algirdas Brazauskas on Wednesday to replace scandal-tainted former finance minister, Rolandas Matiliauskas.
Newspaper Lietuvos rytas quoted Shemeta as saying that it was better to carry out an active monetary policy and that he thought the plans of the central bank to end the currency board were sound.
The litas is currently pegged at four to one dollar under a currency board, which means that any rise in local currency has to be backed by a rise in foreign currency reserves.
It is a crude but effective form of bringing stability and trust to the currency but precludes any active monetary policy on behalf of the central bank.
The country now wants gradually to end the currency board and allow the central bank to manage the fixed peg with money market instruments such as repurchase deals.
The central bank has said that any change to the current peg will not happen earlier than 1999.
Lietuvos rytas quoted Shemeta as saying that it was better to manage monetary policy actively than to have the inflexibility of the present system.
